bullets.title: Semis/AI trade: worst week since 2023 amid neocloud financing fears & CXMT competition
bullets.body: SOX fell 8 consecutive sessions (longest since 2006, down ~11.5% on week); NDX lost ~550bps, worst week since Liberation Day. Key drivers: CRWV CDS spiked to 1,194bp (~60% default odds), Gartner warning $3.5T AI infra at impairment risk by 2030, China's CXMT claiming 4F² DRAM breakthrough ~2 years ahead of Samsung, and AVGO CEO Hock Tan warning capital constraints—not chips—are now the biggest bottleneck. Semis de-rated from ~29x fwd P/E to ~17x; NDX fwd P/E at 20.5x, lowest since AI cycle began. Positioning shakeout vs. fundamental deterioration is the central debate heading into hyperscaler earnings.

bullets.title: NVDA: Hedgeye removes long on Rubin delay; bulls cite fundamentals, sentiment shakeout
bullets.body: Hedgeye removed its NVDA long citing Rubin mass production delayed to Q2 2027 (vs. late Q4/Q1 buyside expectations) and neocloud financing stress threatening GPU demand. Counter-thesis (The AI Bubble Didn't Pop. Hedge Fund Leverage Did.): NVDA stock flat for a year despite earnings beats, fwd P/E compressed to ~15x, H100 GPU rentals higher than a year ago, guided 70% growth. Jensen Huang publicly defended CoreWeave's financial health and called capital costs 'actually decreasing.'

bullets.title: CRWV: Debt stress crystallizes; JPM upgrades to OW, contract economics solid
bullets.body: CoreWeave unsecured bonds fell to ~78¢ (yielding ~15%), CDS spiking to 1,194bp. DA Davidson upgraded to Buy ($110 PT). JPM upgraded to Overweight arguing debt concerns reflect timing of cash flows, not fundamentals: 5-year contract economics generate ~16% residual cash flow, unlevered IRR mid-teens vs. blended cost of capital 9-11%, capacity pre-sold under take-or-pay contracts. Financing costs would need to exceed 20% to neutralize improved unit economics. GPU ASPs up 25% in 3Q with another 10% across the board.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler earnings week: META, AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL are the key clearing events
bullets.body: 13.8% of SPX by market cap reporting next week. JPM top internet picks: META, AMZN, SPOT, GOOGL. GOOGL Cloud growth raised to +100% 3Q on TPU ramp; AMZN AWS modeled +40% 2027 with 2M GPU deployment. META recording $10B legal accrual but seen as overweight on Muse Wonder launch momentum. MSFT Azure expected 46-47% cc growth vs. 44-45% guidance; Azure expected to exit FY27 at 48%+. Jefferies and Morgan Stanley both constructive on MSFT and GOOGL into earnings.

bullets.title: META: Muse Wonder launch drives +40% off lows; 2027 capex/expense debate is key risk
bullets.body: META launched Muse Wonder and Wonder Full, claiming frontier-class performance vs. Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra; Muse held #1 US App Store position. Citi raised PT to $895; UBS to $884; multiple analysts model ~$210B 2027 expenses. GS sees AI-driven ad improvements in creative, targeting, and measurement. Key risks: 2027 capex expected $225-250B vs. Street ~$200B; 3Q includes $10B legal accrual for state AG settlement. Bears flag FCF gap vs. capex through 2028.

bullets.title: NFLX: CCO replacement flags engagement problem; 3Q earnings inline but 2027 debated
bullets.body: Netflix named ex-Fox/Disney exec Peter Rice as Chief Content Officer (effective Oct 26), replacing Bela Bajaria after a decade. Co-CEO Sarandos admitted engagement 'not growing as fast as I want.' Company also cutting ~1K employees (~6% of workforce), largest reduction since 2022. Q3 consensus: $12.87B revenue/$0.82 EPS, ~8.9% implied move. Jefferies maintains Buy at $85 PT on 14%+ EPS CAGR from pricing, ads, and buybacks. Bears cite slowing engagement, rising content costs.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: Shareholders approve Fox acquisition of Roku; FOXA upgraded to Buy at BofA ($85 PT)
bullets.body: Roku shareholders approved Fox's $160/share acquisition ($22B EV); DOJ issued Second Request extending review to H1 2027. BofA upgraded FOXA to Buy from Underperform, raising PT to $85 from $54 (33% upside). Wolfe analysts bullish on the combination but monitoring Roku's longer-term OS share risk—Roku CTV OS share fell ~2 points Y/Y in 1H'26 as Samsung, Vizio, and Amazon Fire gained. Management stopped reporting Roku OS share of new CTV sales.

bullets.title: ACN: Investor Day beats; UBS upgrades to Buy ($278 PT), raises FY29 growth to mid-high single digits
bullets.body: Accenture's first analyst day since 2022 delivered FY27-29 guidance: mid-single digit CC growth FY27-28, accelerating to mid-to-high single digits FY29 (above Street ~+4.8%). Network businesses (~6% of revenue) expected to grow 30%+ CAGR to 12% by FY29. Emerging Alliances revenue doubled YoY with bookings tripling (NVDA, OpenAI, Palantir). Separately, exploring sale of China operations for up to $1.5B per FT. UBS raised PT to $278, JPM raised to OW.

bullets.title: TXN: Earnings catalyst—JPM and UBS see 4Q guidance above Street; data center growing
bullets.body: Texas Instruments reports Oct 21. Buyside expects 4Q guidance flat Q/Q vs. -3% Street consensus. TXN data center business can grow 73-75% Y/Y in CQ3/CQ4. Pricing improving, auto less bad, CE exposure is the main risk. UBS top pick in analog semis; Piper's checks show TXN as positive. Potential short-squeeze catalyst if results beat on pricing/utilization.

bullets.title: WDC: Buyside bar well above Street; $4.25-4.50 Sept EPS vs. consensus $4.09
bullets.body: Western Digital reports Oct 22. Buyside expects Sept quarter EPS $4.25-4.50 vs. consensus $4.09, and Dec guidance $5.10-5.25 vs. consensus $4.77. Memory sector had worst week in 8 sessions—MU, SNDK, WDC each down 7%+ driven by CXMT competition fears and AI sentiment. Micron separately signed agreements covering 35%+ of revenue through 2030; MU IR call showed >75% FY27 supply committed, with discussions already shifting to 2028 allocations and a new $33B buyback.

bullets.title: TEAM: KeyBanc raises PT to $235; usage-based pricing and Rovo driving outperformance
bullets.body: KeyBanc raised Atlassian PT to $235 (from $185) on usage-based pricing catalyst expected to impact 60-80% of customers by year-end, potential for Collections upsell, and Cloud revenue growth potentially accelerating from F4Q's 30.8% Y/Y. Wolfe and Mizuho both constructive: Rovo in nearly every enterprise conversation, JSM solid, migrations accelerating. Raised PTs: NOW to $170, MSFT to $600, TEAM to $235 at Mizuho.

bullets.title: NOW: Strongest enterprise software checks; large deals, PubSec strength, no quarter-end pressure
bullets.body: ServiceNow consistently showed the strongest checks across multiple sell-side surveys: large-deal activity, public sector/federal momentum, no end-of-quarter theatrics. Citi raised PT to $170, Mizuho to $170, Oppenheimer to $165. Piper raised PT to $175 citing Mythos Moment catalysts, M&A outperformance, SKU transition pricing uplift, and ~$1.5B AI ACV target. NOW Q3 print expected strong; 4Q guidance will be the key stock reaction driver.

bullets.title: ANET/networking: AI campus shift bullish; ANET raised FY guidance to $1.1B+, AI Fabrics floor $3.5B
bullets.body: Arista raised FY guidance; AI Fabrics revenue floor $3.5B+, Campus $1.25B+, with scale-up ramp potential in 2027-28. ANET gross margins stable despite cloud mix. OCP 2026 confirmed Ethernet as favored scale-up connectivity standard. CSCO P200 systems in production at Microsoft and Alibaba, G300 sampling. LITE and MTSI most levered to 1.6T transceiver ramp; CRDO's optical portfolio underappreciated. 80M 1.6T transceiver units expected in CY27.

bullets.title: GTLB: Drops 7% on Anthropic Scion fears, recovers; management says Anthropic still a customer
bullets.body: GitLab fell 7% on Oct 13 after Anthropic announced Scion, an internal source control system built because it 'outgrew git.' Sell-side group call with GitLab management clarified: Anthropic remains a GitLab customer, Scion is non-commercial, only applicable to organizations with extremely large code repos, and Anthropic plans to continue partnering with GitLab/GitHub. GTLB recovered within 2 days. Stock trades at 6.1x FY28E EV/Revenue vs. 13x for 20%+ growth software cohort.

bullets.title: OTAs (ABNB/EXPE/BKNG): Agentic AI threat escalates; Hedgeye upgrades ABNB to Best Idea Long, shorts EXPE
bullets.body: OTA stocks down 15-25% following META Muse/Instinct launches that complete full travel bookings via browser automation without OTA intermediation. Hedgeye upgraded ABNB to Best Idea Long ($190-220 target) on hotel push strategy and fragmented inventory advantage; maintains EXPE on Short Bias (tough comps, B2B sustainability concerns); BKNG neutral. MS webcast concluded distribution deflation could drive lodging estimate inflation—every 100bps shift to direct adds 10-50bps EBITDA for hotel owners.

bullets.title: FICO/EFX/TRU: Mizuho cuts PTs on mortgage headwinds and VS4 competition
bullets.body: Mizuho cut PTs citing MBA mortgage app index -14% Y/Y in Q3, refinancing down -22%, and VantageScore 4.0 share rising to ~4.8% of GSE mortgages (Rocket ~32%, UWM ~24%). FICO PT cut to $1,063 from $1,344; EFX to $185 from $210; TRU to $74 from $77. EFX government verification accelerating (+$100M new bookings). Bi-merge transition affects <5% of EFX/TRU revenues. Regulatory overhang likely driving valuation pressure.

bullets.title: SHOP: Price increases 13-20% on new annual plans signal pricing power; agentic commerce bull case intact
bullets.body: Shopify raised Grow/Advanced tier pricing ~13-20% for new annual plans only; Basic tier also increased ex-US. UBS estimates immaterial 2027 impact but views as confirmation of pricing power, aligned with CFO comments. JPM maintained Overweight at $200 PT with ~30% 2027E revenue growth path and agentic commerce bull case. Expert call with Shopify Platinum partner Zettler Digital on AI-commerce strategy, SMB demand, and Merchant Solutions adoption scheduled Oct 19.

bullets.title: T: AT&T sells Mexico wireless for $2B; Bernstein downgrades on Starlink risk
bullets.body: AT&T agreed to sell AT&T Mexico to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2B in cash (2.3x EV/EBITDA), closing Q1 2027. Bernstein downgraded to Market Perform ($24 PT from $25) citing ongoing pressure from SpaceX Starlink's spectrum acquisition (800MHz from Grain Management) and Q4 seasonality. Morgan Stanley reiterated OW, viewing the telecom selloff as overdone; SpaceX more likely a network-based competitor than direct carrier.

bullets.title: TSLA: MS turns more constructive post-Cybercab launch; new Roadster unveiled
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley turned more constructive on Tesla, citing 300+ Cybercabs in Austin over 30 days and 1M+ unsupervised miles as robotaxi density catalysts. MS PT $400. Tesla also unveiled a new Roadster with air thruster capabilities (SpaceX thrusters), 0-60 in 1 second, targeting 2028 production. Hedgeye Risk Range shifted TSLA from Bullish to Neutral on Oct 15. Flying car speculation intensified Tesla-SpaceX merger discussion.

bullets.title: BE: $4B AEP/Google 702MW fuel cell deal validates commercial momentum; Morgan Stanley OW Top Pick
bullets.body: AEP announced ~$4B investment in a 702MW Bloom Energy fuel cell project near Cheyenne, Wyoming, under a 20-year PPA with Google. Construction starts 2026, fully operational by end-2028. Morgan Stanley rates BE Overweight and as a Top Pick; Equinix also OW Top Pick. Roth raised PT to $260 from $225 (Neutral). Schneider Electric reported triple-digit data center demand growth—positive read-through for VRT, FPS, GEV, BE.
